title: Back to the Future: Modern, Parametric Manual Plunge-Freezer for Cryo-EM
content: The most popular method of sample preparation for cryo-TEM, blotting and plunge-freezing, has remained largely unchanged for several decades – a popularity that stems in large part from its conceptual simplicity [1,2]. However, the original ad-hoc implementations of this approach never reached broad adoption as they require fabrication and design experience outside that of typical structural biology research groups. The last two decades, however, have seen a rapid advancement in the accessibility of manufacturing technologies and services (i.e. improved CAD software, CNC machining, rapid-prototyping shops, 3D printing, etc.). Here, we describe a cost-effective manual plunge-freezer that can be produced for less than a tenth of the cost of commercially available equipment and is organized as an open-hardware project that can draw further involvement and improvement from the community. In addition, this project also aims to provide these plans as parametric models that can be easily adjusted to accommodate variations and/or improvements in parts. Our motivation is to offer a low-cost, accessible solution for cryo-TEM sample preparation that serves as a teaching aid, an entry point for novice users, and an essential tool for advanced practitioners. The files and instructions are available for free download on PNCC’s website [3].
